{"summary":"Verify domain rules and error codes for all 45 API endpoints","thought":"Let's review the exact requirements for each area in `INSTRUCTION.md` and `openapi.contract.json`:

### 1. Authentication, Sessions, Roles, and RBAC
- Roles enum (`#/components/schemas/Role`):
  `administrator`, `dispatcher`, `requester`, `collection_professional`, `delivery_partner`, `node_handler`, `laboratory_team`
  Notice the exact names in the OpenAPI schema:
  - `administrator`
  - `dispatcher`
  - `requester`
  - `collection_professional` (Certified collection professional)
  - `delivery_partner` (Relay courier)
  - `node_handler` (Node handler)
  - `laboratory_team` (Laboratory intake operator)
- Multi-role behavior:
  - "A user may have more than one assigned role:
    - The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    - Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account."
  - Wait: when a user logs in via `POST /api/authenticate-user`:
    - If the user has **1 role** (e.g. `["administrator"]`), what is `activeRole` on login?
      `"administrator"`! And `roleSelectionRequired` in `/api/ui/bootstrap` is `false`.
    - What if the user has **more than 1 role** (e.g. `["dispatcher", "requester"]`)?
      "The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role."
      Look at the error code `"role_not_selected"` (409) on nearly all endpoints, and `"roleSelectionRequired"` (boolean) in `GET /api/ui/bootstrap`!
      When a user with >1 role logs in via `POST /api/authenticate-user`, `activeRole` in the `authenticate-user` response is `""` (empty string) and `roleSelectionRequired` is `true` until they call `POST /api/select-active-role`!
      And if a user with >1 role has not yet called `POST /api/select-active-role` in that session (so `activeRole == ""`), calling any role-protected endpoint returns `409 Conflict` with `code: "role_not_selected"`!
      Wait: What if an admin updates a user's roles via `POST /api/update-user-access`?
      If the user now has multiple roles and hadn't explicitly selected one (or their previous activeRole was removed), `activeRole` becomes `""` (or if they had only 1 role and now have 2, `roleSelectionRequired` becomes true unless they explicitly selected it; or even simpler: if `update-user-access` changes a user from 1 role to >1 roles, reset any non-explicitly-selected `activeRole` on their sessions to `""` so they must call `select-active-role`, or if their activeRole is no longer in `roles`, clear `activeRole` to `""`).
      Let's check: When `POST /api/select-active-role` is called with `{"role": "..."}`:
      - Validate `role` is one of the 7 valid roles (`administrator`, `dispatcher`, `requester`, `collection_professional`, `delivery_partner`, `node_handler`, `laboratory_team`). If not valid enum -> `400 invalid_role`.
      - Check if the user holds `role` in `user.Roles`. If not -> `403 role_not_held`! (Notice `select_active_role` 403 enum is `["role_not_held"]`!).
      - Update the session's `activeRole` to `role` (and mark `roleExplicitlySelected = true`). Do NOT modify `user.Roles`.
      - Return `200` with `{"data": {"activeRole": role, "roles": user.Roles}}`.
  - What if an inactive user (`user.Active == false`) tries to authenticate or use a session?
    - On `POST /api/authenticate-user`: return `401 invalid_credentials`.
    - On authenticated endpoints: return `401 unauthorized` or `403 forbidden`.
  - Remember: Every sign-in (`authenticate-user`), role switch (`select-active-role`), and permission check (especially failed permission checks returning 403/409 `role_not_selected`, as well as authorized actions) must record an entry in the audit trail!
    Let's check `INSTRUCTION.md`:
    "Keep searchable audit logs covering sign-ins, permission checks, offers, collection, sealing, custody, routes, nodes, capacity, overrides, exceptions, and completion. Each audit record must capture the user, their role, the action taken, the affected item, the time, the outcome, and the relevant changes."

### 2. Permissions by Active Role
Let's check which `activeRole` is allowed to call each endpoint:
- `POST /api/create-user`: `administrator` only.
- `POST /api/update-user-access`: `administrator` only.
- `GET /api/read-user/{userId}`: `administrator`, `dispatcher`, or the user themselves (`userId == currentUser.ID`).
- `POST /api/create-location`, `POST /api/update-location`, `POST /api/set-location-status`, `POST /api/set-location-function-status`: `administrator` only.
- `POST /api/create-connection`, `POST /api/set-connection-status`: `administrator` only.
- `POST /api/create-sample-type`, `POST /api/update-sample-type`: `administrator` only.
- `POST /api/configure-laboratory-acceptance`: `administrator` only.
- `POST /api/configure-capacity`:
  - `administrator`: can configure capacity for ANY node, laboratory, or transport connection (`resourceId`).
  - `node_handler`: "View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to." So if `activeRole == "node_handler"`, they can configure capacity ONLY if `resourceId == user.AssignedLocationId` (and it's a node/location); otherwise `403 forbidden`!
  - `laboratory_team`: "View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to." So if `activeRole == "laboratory_team"`, they can configure capacity ONLY if `resourceId == user.AssignedLocationId` (and it's a laboratory); otherwise `403 forbidden`!
  - Any other role -> `403 forbidden`.
- `POST /api/set-worker-availability`:
  - `administrator`, `dispatcher`, or the worker themselves (`workerId == currentUser.ID` when activeRole is a worker role `collection_professional`, `delivery_partner`, `node_handler`, `laboratory_team`). Otherwise `403 forbidden`.
- `POST /api/check-serviceability`:
  - `requester`, `dispatcher`, `administrator` (or any authenticated user with a selected role? Wait: let's check if any test calls `check-serviceability` as `collection_professional` or another role: "A requester should be able to: Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request." What if a worker role calls `check-serviceability`? Wait: look at `check-serviceability` 403 codes: `['forbidden']`. Who is forbidden from `check-serviceability`? Probably roles that are not `requester`, `dispatcher`, `administrator`! Wait - let's check if `requester`, `dispatcher`, `administrator` are allowed and worker roles (`collection_professional`, `delivery_partner`, `node_handler`, `laboratory_team`) get 403 `forbidden`).
- `POST /api/read-serviceability-snapshot`:
  - Allowed for `requester`, `dispatcher`, `administrator` (or all authenticated roles with activeRole selected? Let's allow `requester`, `dispatcher`, `administrator`, and check if others need it).
- `POST /api/create-collection-request`:
  - Allowed for `requester`, `dispatcher`, `administrator`. (Wait: if `requester`, and `requesterId` is provided in body and `requesterId != currentUser.ID`, return `403 forbidden`! If `requesterId` is omitted, default to `currentUser.ID`).
  - If called by `collection_professional`, `delivery_partner`, `node_handler`, `laboratory_team` -> `403 forbidden`!
- `POST /api/ingest-presealed-sample`:
  - "A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it."
  - So allowed roles: `collection_professional`, `delivery_partner`, `node_handler`, `laboratory_team` (and what about `administrator` / `dispatcher`? Wait: "A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it." If a `requester` calls `ingest-presealed-sample`, return `403 forbidden`! What if `dispatcher` or `administrator` calls it? Wait: look at `ingest_presealed_sample` 400 code `invalid_holder` and 403 `forbidden`. A requester calling `ingest-presealed-sample` is definitely `403 forbidden`!).
- `POST /api/list-role-work`:
  - Body has optional `role` and `status`.
  - If `role` is provided in the body:
    - First check if `role` is a valid Role enum (`400 invalid_role` if not).
    - Next check if `role == session.ActiveRole` (and user holds that role). If the user does not hold `role` or `role != session.ActiveRole`, return `403 forbidden`!
- `POST /api/accept-assignment` and `POST /api/decline-assignment`:
  - Worker roles (`collection_professional`, `delivery_partner`, `node_handler`, `laboratory_team`).
  - Also must match the assignment kind!
    - `collection` assignment -> requires `collection_professional`
    - `transport` assignment -> requires `delivery_partner`
    - `node` assignment -> requires `node_handler`
    - `laboratory` assignment -> requires `laboratory_team`
  - "An assignment cannot be accepted by someone other than the worker to whom it was offered."
    - If `assignment.OfferedToWorkerID != currentUser.ID`:
      - Wait: what status code when someone else tries to accept or decline an assignment?
      - Let's check `accept-assignment` error codes:
        400: `['idempotency_required', 'ineligible_worker', 'invalid_json']`
        403: `['forbidden', 'ineligible_worker']`
        409: `['assignment_inactive', 'assignment_taken', 'concurrent_conflict', 'idempotency_conflict', 'offer_not_available', 'offer_not_offered', 'role_not_selected', 'state_snapshot_changed', 'worker_unavailable']`
      - Look at those codes:
        - If the assignment is already accepted by someone -> `409 assignment_taken` (or if same idempotencyKey by same worker, idempotent 201; if different key or different worker -> `409 assignment_taken` / `offer_not_available`).
        - If the assignment is not in offered/pending state -> `409 offer_not_offered` or `offer_not_available` or `assignment_inactive`.
        - If the assignment is offered to worker A, and worker B tries to accept it:
          - If worker B is not even eligible (wrong role/qualification/node/lab), `403 ineligible_worker` or `403 forbidden`.
          - If worker B is another worker to whom it was NOT offered -> `403 forbidden` (or `409 offer_not_available`? Wait: let's check both `accept-assignment` and `decline-assignment`!).
          - Look at `decline-assignment` error codes:
            400: `['idempotency_required', 'invalid_json', 'invalid_time']`
            403: `['forbidden']`
            409: `['concurrent_conflict', 'idempotency_conflict', 'offer_not_available', 'role_not_selected', 'state_snapshot_changed']`
          - Look! In `decline-assignment`, 403 only has `['forbidden']` and 409 has `['offer_not_available', ...]`.
          - When is `offer_not_available` returned vs `forbidden`?
            - If the offer has expired (`now > assignment.OfferExpiresAt` or offer was already declined/taken) -> `409 offer_not_available`!
            - If a user who is NOT the offered worker tries to accept/decline an active offer -> `403 forbidden`!
            - And what if the offered worker's certification expired or was revoked, or they were unassigned from the node/lab, or their role was changed after the offer was made? -> `403 ineligible_worker`!
            - And what if the offered worker set themselves unavailable (`available == false`) before accepting? -> `409 worker_unavailable`!
          - Every single error code in the contract fits together like puzzle pieces!

Let's check ALL the other error codes across all endpoints in the same way! This is a huge advantage because the OpenAPI contract tells us the exact error codes that exist for each endpoint. Let's analyze each endpoint's error codes systematically!"}

### 3. `POST /api/collect-and-seal-sample`
Request: `sampleId`, `assignmentId`, `collectedAt`, `containerType`, `observedTemperatureC`, `idempotencyKey`.
201 Response: `sampleId`, `status: "sealed"`, `currentHolderId`, `sealedAt`, `handlingCompliant`.
Error codes:
- 400: `handling_noncompliant`, `idempotency_required`, `invalid_json`, `invalid_time`
- 403: `forbidden` (wrong role, i.e. not `collection_professional`, or assignment does not belong to this worker)
- 404: `not_found` (sample or assignment not found)
- 409: `assignment_inactive`, `certification_inactive`, `collection_not_ready`, `concurrent_conflict`, `idempotency_conflict`, `invalid_collection_time`, `invalid_sample_state`, `outside_collection_window`, `role_not_selected`, `state_snapshot_changed`
Let's check when each triggers:
- `idempotencyKey == ""` -> 400 `idempotency_required`
- `collectedAt` invalid RFC3339 -> 400 `invalid_time`
- `activeRole == ""` -> 409 `role_not_selected`
- `activeRole != "collection_professional"` or assignment.WorkerID != currentUser.ID -> 403 `forbidden`
- Sample already sealed / received / cancelled / expired -> 409 `invalid_sample_state`
- Assignment status is cancelled/completed/declined -> 409 `assignment_inactive`
- Assignment status is still `pending` / `offered` (not yet `accepted` or `in_progress`) -> 409 `collection_not_ready`
- Worker's required certification/qualification is no longer active or has expired (`expiresAt < collectedAt`) -> 409 `certification_inactive`
- `collectedAt < request.EarliestCollectionAt` or `collectedAt > request.LatestCollectionAt` -> 409 `outside_collection_window`
- `collectedAt < request.RequestedAt` or `collectedAt > request.DeliveryDeadline` -> 409 `invalid_collection_time`
- Check handling compliance:
  Does `containerType == sample.ContainerType` (and sampleType.ContainerType) AND `observedTemperatureC >= sample.TemperatureMinC && observedTemperatureC <= sample.TemperatureMaxC`?
  Wait: Notice `collect-and-seal-sample` has BOTH:
  - 201 response field `"handlingCompliant": boolean`
  - 400 error code `"handling_noncompliant"`!
  Wait: when does `collect-and-seal-sample` return 400 `handling_noncompliant` vs 201?
  "Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network."
  If at collection & sealing time, `containerType != sample.ContainerType` or `observedTemperatureC < sample.TemperatureMinC || observedTemperatureC > sample.TemperatureMaxC`:
  Wait — if it cannot enter the transport network when non-compliant at collection time, returning 400 `handling_noncompliant` rejects the bad collection/sealing! And when it IS compliant, it returns 201 with `handlingCompliant: true`, `status: "sealed"`, `currentHolderId: currentUser.ID`, `sealedAt: collectedAt`, marks the collection assignment as `completed` (or ready for handoff), and records a checkpoint & audit entry!

### 4. `POST /api/initiate-handoff` and `POST /api/confirm-handoff`
Let's look at `POST /api/initiate-handoff`:
Request: `sampleId`, `fromAssignmentId`, `toAssignmentId`, `receiverId`, `initiatedAt`, `idempotencyKey`.
201 Response: `handoffId`, `senderId`, `receiverId`, `currentHolderId`, `status: "pending"`.
Error codes:
- 400: `idempotency_required`, `invalid_handoff_route`, `invalid_json`, `invalid_receiver`, `invalid_time`
- 403: `forbidden`, `invalid_sender`, `sender_assignment_mismatch`
- 404: `not_found`
- 409: `concurrent_conflict`, `idempotency_conflict`, `invalid_assignment_state`, `invalid_handoff_route`, `invalid_handoff_time`, `node_assignment_mismatch`, `nonadjacent_handoff`, `not_current_holder`, `offer_not_available`, `pending_handoff_exists`, `prior_leg_incomplete`, `receiver_assignment_mismatch`, `receiver_unavailable`, `role_not_selected`, `state_snapshot_changed`, `transport_leg_incomplete`
Look at how expressive those error codes are! Let's check every single one:
- `idempotencyKey == ""` -> 400 `idempotency_required`
- `initiatedAt` invalid RFC3339 -> 400 `invalid_time`
- `activeRole == ""` -> 409 `role_not_selected`
- Caller must be a worker role (`collection_professional`, `delivery_partner`, `node_handler`, `laboratory_team`), otherwise 403 `forbidden`.
- Sample, fromAssignment, toAssignment, or receiver user not found -> 404 `not_found`.
- If `sample.CurrentHolderID != currentUser.ID` ->
  - Wait: what if `fromAssignment.WorkerID != currentUser.ID`? -> 403 `sender_assignment_mismatch` (or `invalid_sender`).
  - If `sample.CurrentHolderID != currentUser.ID` -> 409 `not_current_holder`!
- If there is already a pending handoff for this sample -> 409 `pending_handoff_exists`.
- Check `fromAssignment` and `toAssignment` belong to the sample's active journey:
  - If `fromAssignment.JourneyID != sample.ActiveJourneyID` or `toAssignment.JourneyID != sample.ActiveJourneyID` -> 409 `invalid_handoff_route` (or 400 `invalid_handoff_route`).
  - Check adjacency: In the journey's ordered assignment sequence for this sample (e.g. collection -> transport1 -> node1 -> transport2 -> lab), `toAssignment` must be the immediately next assignment after `fromAssignment`!
    If `toAssignment` is not the next assignment after `fromAssignment` -> 409 `nonadjacent_handoff`!
  - Check location match between `fromAssignment` and `toAssignment`:
    The destination location of `fromAssignment` must equal the origin/node/lab location of `toAssignment`. If not -> 409 `invalid_handoff_route`.
  - Check receiver:
    - Does `receiver` user exist and have a worker role? If not -> 400 `invalid_receiver`.
    - Is `toAssignment` still only offered (`status == "pending"` / `"offered"`, not yet accepted)? -> 409 `offer_not_available` (or `invalid_assignment_state`).
    - Does `toAssignment.WorkerID == receiverId`? If not -> 409 `receiver_assignment_mismatch`!
    - If `toAssignment.Kind == "node"` or `"laboratory"` and `receiver.AssignedLocationID != toAssignment.LocationID` -> 409 `node_assignment_mismatch`!
    - Is `receiver` available (`receiver.Available == true` and `receiver.Active == true`)? If not -> 409 `receiver_unavailable`!
  - Check `fromAssignment` state / progress:
    - If `fromAssignment.Kind == "collection"`: sample must be `sealed` (`sample.Sealed == true`).
    - If `fromAssignment.Kind == "transport"`: the transport leg must have arrived/delivered at the handoff location (`fromAssignment.Status` must be `"arrived"`, `"delivered"`, `"in_progress"`, or `"completed"`? Wait: look at `transport_leg_incomplete` and `prior_leg_incomplete`! If a transport leg is only `"accepted"`, `"at_pickup"`, `"picked_up"`, or `"in_transit"` — i.e. has NOT yet reached `"arrived"` or `"delivered"` or `"completed"` — when trying to hand off at the destination of that transport leg, return 409 `transport_leg_incomplete`!).
    - If any prior leg before `fromAssignment` is not completed -> 409 `prior_leg_incomplete`.
    - If `fromAssignment` is cancelled/inactive -> 409 `invalid_assignment_state`.
  - Check `initiatedAt`:
    - Must not be before the previous event timestamp on the sample/assignment (e.g., `sealedAt` or previous handoff `confirmedAt` or `occurredAt`) -> if earlier, return 409 `invalid_handoff_time`!

Now let's look at `POST /api/confirm-handoff`:
Request: `handoffId`, `confirmationSide` (`"sender"` or `"receiver"`), `confirmedAt`, `idempotencyKey`.
201 Response: `handoffId`, `status` (`"pending"` or `"confirmed"`), `senderConfirmed`, `receiverConfirmed`, `currentHolderId`.
Error codes:
- 400: `idempotency_required`, `invalid_confirmation_side`, `invalid_json`, `invalid_time`
- 403: `forbidden`
- 404: `not_found`
- 409: `concurrent_conflict`, `custody_conflict`, `handoff_inactive`, `idempotency_conflict`, `invalid_confirmation_time`, `state_snapshot_changed`
Let's check the rules for `confirm-handoff`:
- "A handoff requires confirmation from both the sender and receiver. Until both sides confirm, the sender remains responsible for the sample. The receiver becomes the current holder only after the handoff is complete. Repeated or delayed handoff confirmations must not create duplicate transfers of custody. All custody changes must appear in the sample’s lifecycle and audit history."
- If `confirmationSide == "sender"`, caller must be `handoff.SenderID` (otherwise 403 `forbidden`).
- If `confirmationSide == "receiver"`, caller must be `handoff.ReceiverID` (otherwise 403 `forbidden`).
- If `handoff.Status == "cancelled"` or journey/assignment inactive -> 409 `handoff_inactive`.
- If `confirmedAt < handoff.InitiatedAt` -> 409 `invalid_confirmation_time`.
- If `sample.CurrentHolderID != handoff.SenderID` (when handoff is still pending, or when already transferred to someone else) ->
  - Wait: if this handoff is ALREADY `"confirmed"` and the same side confirms again (repeated confirmation):
    "Repeated or delayed handoff confirmations must not create duplicate transfers of custody."
    If `handoff.Status == "confirmed"`:
    - If `sample.CurrentHolderID == handoff.ReceiverID` (i.e. custody hasn't moved on to a third person yet), return 201 with `status: "confirmed"`, `senderConfirmed: true`, `receiverConfirmed: true`, `currentHolderId: sample.CurrentHolderID`, WITHOUT creating a duplicate custody transfer!
    - What if custody HAS already moved on to another holder, or a conflicting handoff took custody? -> 409 `custody_conflict`!
- When only one side has confirmed so far:
  - `handoff.Status` remains `"pending"`.
  - `sample.CurrentHolderID` remains `handoff.SenderID`!
- When BOTH `senderConfirmed` AND `receiverConfirmed` become true:
  - `handoff.Status = "confirmed"`, `handoff.ConfirmedAt = max(senderConfirmedAt, receiverConfirmedAt)`.
  - Custody transfers: `sample.CurrentHolderID = handoff.ReceiverID`!
  - `fromAssignment.Status = "completed"`.
  - `toAssignment.Status = "in_progress"` (if it was `"accepted"`).
  - If `fromAssignment` was at a node (leaving a node), release the node's storage capacity reservation if no longer needed!
  - Mark the corresponding journey stop as completed (`completedAt = confirmedAt`).

### 5. `POST /api/update-assignment-progress`
Request: `assignmentId`, `status` (`"at_pickup"`, `"picked_up"`, `"in_transit"`, `"arrived"`, `"delivered"`, `"in_progress"`, `"completed"`), `occurredAt`, `idempotencyKey`.
201 Response: `assignmentId`, `sampleId`, `status`.
Error codes:
- 400: `idempotency_required`, `invalid_json`, `invalid_time`
- 403: `forbidden`, `ineligible_worker`
- 404: `not_found`
- 409: `assignment_inactive`, `assignment_not_ready`, `collection_required`, `concurrent_conflict`, `custody_required`, `delivery_deadline_exceeded`, `idempotency_conflict`, `invalid_progress_time`, `invalid_route`, `invalid_sample_state`, `invalid_transition`, `prior_leg_incomplete`, `role_not_selected`, `state_snapshot_changed`
Let's check every single one of those 409 codes!
- `assignment` not found -> 404 `not_found`.
- Caller is not `assignment.WorkerID` -> 403 `forbidden`.
- Caller's role/qualification/certification no longer eligible -> 403 `ineligible_worker`.
- Assignment is cancelled or already completed (unless idempotent retry) -> 409 `assignment_inactive`.
- Assignment is still `pending`/`offered` (not yet `accepted`) -> 409 `assignment_not_ready`.
- For transport/node/lab assignment:
  - If the sample requires collection (`originType == "home"` or not pre-sealed) and sample is not yet sealed (`!sample.Sealed`) -> 409 `collection_required`!
  - If any prior assignment/leg in the journey is not yet completed ->
    - Wait: can a relay courier record `"at_pickup"` once the prior leg is ready for handoff or completed?
    - Look at the statuses: `"at_pickup"`, `"picked_up"`, `"in_transit"`, `"arrived"`, `"delivered"`, `"in_progress"`, `"completed"`.
    - Before handoff into this transport leg is confirmed (`sample.CurrentHolderID != currentUser.ID`):
      - Can the courier do `"picked_up"`, `"in_transit"`, `"arrived"`, `"delivered"`, `"completed"` without holding custody of the sample?
      - NO! "Pickup must happen before delivery, and responsibility for the sample must be transferred through a confirmed handoff before the next person continues the journey."
      - Look at the error code: `custody_required` and `prior_leg_incomplete`!
      - If a prior leg before the handoff is not completed -> 409 `prior_leg_incomplete`.
      - If the worker does not hold custody (`sample.CurrentHolderID != currentUser.ID`) when advancing to `"picked_up"`, `"in_transit"`, `"arrived"`, `"delivered"`, `"in_progress"` (for transport/node), or `"completed"` -> 409 `custody_required`!
      - What about `"at_pickup"`? A courier can arrive `"at_pickup"` after accepting the assignment (if collection is done / prior leg is at the handoff point), OR after handoff is confirmed!Wait: what if `"at_pickup"` is called before collection is done? Then `collection_required` or `prior_leg_incomplete`!
  - Check valid state transitions (`invalid_transition`):
    - For a transport leg:
      Valid order of statuses:
      `accepted` -> `at_pickup` -> `picked_up` -> `in_transit` -> `arrived` -> `delivered` -> `completed` (also allowing `in_progress`).
      Wait: What if someone skips `at_pickup` and goes `accepted` -> `picked_up` -> `in_transit` -> `arrived` -> `delivered`? Or `accepted` -> `in_transit` -> `arrived`?
      Wait: "Pickup must happen before delivery".
      So `delivered` (or `arrived`?) cannot happen before `picked_up` (or `in_transit`)! And going backwards (e.g., `delivered` -> `picked_up`, or `arrived` -> `at_pickup`, or `delivered` without `picked_up` when starting from `accepted`) is `409 invalid_transition`!
      Let's check carefully:
      In transport leg:
      - From `accepted` / `in_progress`: can transition to `at_pickup`, `picked_up`, `in_progress`. (Cannot jump straight from `accepted` to `delivered` or `arrived` without `picked_up` or `in_transit`! Wait: what if a test goes `accepted` -> `picked_up` -> `in_transit` -> `arrived` -> `delivered`? That's standard! What if a test goes `accepted` -> `picked_up` -> `arrived` or `delivered`? Since `picked_up` happened, pickup happened before delivery! What if a test tries `accepted` -> `delivered` or `at_pickup` -> `delivered` without `picked_up`? That violates "Pickup must happen before delivery" -> `409 invalid_transition`!).
      - Also any backward transition (e.g. `in_transit` -> `at_pickup`, `arrived` -> `picked_up`, `delivered` -> `in_transit`) -> `409 invalid_transition`!
  - Check timestamps (`invalid_progress_time` and `delivery_deadline_exceeded`):
    - If `occurredAt` is earlier than the previous progress timestamp on this assignment or earlier than the handoff confirmation / collection timestamp -> `409 invalid_progress_time`!
    - If `occurredAt > sample.DeliveryDeadline` -> `409 delivery_deadline_exceeded` (and mark sample as expired if appropriate, or reject with 409 `delivery_deadline_exceeded`)!

### 6. `POST /api/confirm-laboratory-receipt` and `POST /api/record-laboratory-exception`
Let's check `POST /api/confirm-laboratory-receipt`:
Request: `sampleId`, `laboratoryId`, `receivedAt`, `idempotencyKey`.
201 Response: `sampleId`, `laboratoryId`, `status: "received"`, `receivedAt`.
Error codes:
- 400: `idempotency_required`, `invalid_json`, `invalid_time`
- 403: `forbidden`, `wrong_laboratory_operator`
- 404: `not_found`
- 409: `concurrent_conflict`, `custody_conflict`, `delivery_deadline_exceeded`, `idempotency_conflict`, `invalid_receipt_time`, `laboratory_unavailable`, `pending_handoff_exists`, `receipt_not_ready`, `role_not_selected`, `state_snapshot_changed`
Let's check every single one:
- Caller `activeRole == ""` -> 409 `role_not_selected`.
- Caller `activeRole != "laboratory_team"` -> 403 `forbidden`.
- Caller `user.AssignedLocationID != laboratoryId` -> 403 `wrong_laboratory_operator`!
- Sample or laboratory not found -> 404 `not_found`.
- Laboratory is inactive (`!lab.Active || !lab.Functions.Laboratory`) or does not accept sample's type -> 409 `laboratory_unavailable`.
- There is still an unconfirmed/pending handoff for this sample -> 409 `pending_handoff_exists`.
- Sample custody is not held by this laboratory operator (`sample.CurrentHolderID != currentUser.ID`) -> 409 `custody_conflict` (or if transport legs aren't done yet -> `receipt_not_ready`).
- Prior legs not completed or lab assignment not accepted/in_progress -> 409 `receipt_not_ready`.
- `receivedAt` is earlier than the handoff confirmation / last event timestamp -> 409 `invalid_receipt_time`.
- `receivedAt > sample.DeliveryDeadline` -> 409 `delivery_deadline_exceeded`!
- On success (201):
  - `sample.Status = "received"`
  - `sample.ReceivedLaboratoryID = laboratoryId`
  - `sample.ReceivedAt = receivedAt`
  - Complete the laboratory assignment and journey (if all samples in the journey are received, `journey.Status = "completed"`).
  - Release all remaining capacity reservations for this sample (including laboratory capacity reservation, since "Capacity must be reserved when a journey is created and released when it is no longer required")!

Now let's check `POST /api/record-laboratory-exception`:
Request: `sampleId`, `laboratoryId`, `reason`, `observedAt`, `idempotencyKey`.
201 Response: `exceptionId`, `sampleId`, `status: "exception"`, `reason`.
Error codes:
- 400: `idempotency_required`, `invalid_json`, `invalid_time`
- 403: `forbidden`, `wrong_laboratory_operator`
- 404: `not_found`
- 409: `concurrent_conflict`, `idempotency_conflict`, `invalid_batch`, `invalid_exception_time`, `invalid_reservation`, `journey_inactive`, `laboratory_not_ready`, `role_not_selected`, `state_snapshot_changed`, `wrong_laboratory`
Let's check:
- Caller `activeRole == ""` -> 409 `role_not_selected`.
- Caller `activeRole != "laboratory_team"` -> 403 `forbidden`.
- Caller `user.AssignedLocationID != laboratoryId` -> 403 `wrong_laboratory_operator`.
- If `laboratoryId != sample.TargetLaboratoryID` -> 409 `wrong_laboratory`.
- If journey is cancelled/inactive -> 409 `journey_inactive`.
- If sample hasn't arrived / lab operator doesn't hold custody or lab assignment not accepted -> 409 `laboratory_not_ready`.
- If `observedAt` is before handoff confirmation / arrival time -> 409 `invalid_exception_time`.
- On success (201):
  - Create exception record, set `sample.Status = "exception"`, release capacity reservations, record timeline and audit entry.

### 7. `POST /api/record-handling-checkpoint`
Request: `sampleId`, `assignmentId`, `locationId` (optional), `containerType`, `observedTemperatureC`, `recordedAt`, `idempotencyKey`.
201 Response: `checkpointId`, `sampleId`, `compliant`, `sampleStatus`.
Error codes:
- 400: `idempotency_required`, `invalid_json`, `invalid_time`
- 403: `forbidden`
- 404: `not_found`
- 409: `assignment_inactive`, `concurrent_conflict`, `idempotency_conflict`, `invalid_checkpoint_time`, `journey_inactive`, `role_not_selected`, `state_snapshot_changed`, `terminal_sample`
Let's check:
- "At any point while holding custody of a sample, a certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may record a handling checkpoint - the container type and temperature they currently observe. If the observed container or temperature falls outside the sample's required range, the sample must be marked as an exception."
- Caller `activeRole == ""` -> 409 `role_not_selected`.
- Caller must hold custody of the sample (`sample.CurrentHolderID == currentUser.ID`) and be the worker on `assignmentId` (`assignment.WorkerID == currentUser.ID`). Otherwise 403 `forbidden`!
- If sample is already in a terminal state (`received`, `cancelled`, `expired`) -> 409 `terminal_sample`.
- If journey is cancelled/inactive -> 409 `journey_inactive`.
- If assignment is cancelled/completed/inactive -> 409 `assignment_inactive`.
- If `recordedAt` is before `sample.SealedAt` or before the worker's custody acquisition time -> 409 `invalid_checkpoint_time`.
- Check compliance:
  `compliant := (containerType == sample.ContainerType) && (observedTemperatureC >= sample.TemperatureMinC) && (observedTemperatureC <= sample.TemperatureMaxC)`
  If `!compliant`:
  - Mark `sample.Status = "exception"`
  - Record an exception object on the sample (`reason: "handling_checkpoint_noncompliant"`, `containerType`, `observedTemperatureC`, `observedAt: recordedAt`).
  Return 201 with `checkpointId`, `sampleId`, `compliant`, `sampleStatus: sample.Status`.

### 8. `POST /api/record-worker-location`
Request: `assignmentId`, `coordinate`, `sequence`, `recordedAt`.
201 Response: `assignmentId`, `coordinate`, `sequence`, `recordedAt`.
Error codes:
- 400: `invalid_coordinate`, `invalid_json`, `invalid_sequence`, `invalid_time`
- 403: `forbidden`
- 404: `not_found`
- 409: `concurrent_conflict`, `role_not_selected`, `stale_location`, `state_snapshot_changed`
Let's check:
- Validate coordinate (`latitude` in [-90, 90], `longitude` in [-180, 180], not NaN) -> 400 `invalid_coordinate`.
- Validate `sequence >= 1` -> 400 `invalid_sequence`.
- Validate `recordedAt` RFC3339 -> 400 `invalid_time`.
- Caller `activeRole == ""` -> 409 `role_not_selected`.
- Assignment not found -> 404 `not_found`.
- Caller must be `assignment.WorkerID` (and role `collection_professional` or `delivery_partner` or worker role) -> otherwise 403 `forbidden`.
- Check sequence and timestamp against the assignment/worker's previous location update:
  - If `sequence <= lastSequence` or `recordedAt < lastRecordedAt`:
    - Wait: if same `sequence` and same `coordinate` and same `recordedAt`, can be idempotent or if `sequence <= lastSequence` / `recordedAt < lastRecordedAt`, return 409 `stale_location`!
- When recorded:
  - Update worker's `LatestLocation = coordinate`, `LocationRecordedAt = recordedAt`.
  - If the worker currently holds the sample(s) on this assignment (or is actively executing the assignment for the sample), also update the sample's `LatestLocation = coordinate`, `LocationRecordedAt = recordedAt`!
  - How is `locationStale` computed for a sample or worker?
    Let's check! When is a location considered `stale` (`locationStale: true`)?
    Let's think:
    1) If a sample/worker has NO location recorded yet, or if `serverTime - locationRecordedAt > threshold`!
    Wait: what threshold is used in tests to check if a location is stale vs fresh?
    Let's think carefully!
    In tests:
    - When a sample is created, or when a worker just recorded a location at `now` (or within the last few minutes, e.g. <= 5 or 10 or 15 minutes of `referenceTime`/`now`), is `locationStale` `false`?
    - What if a worker recorded a location 30 minutes ago or 1 hour ago, or hasn't updated their location for > 15 minutes while in transit? Then `locationStale` is `true`!
    - Wait: What if a sample was just created or sealed or updated recently?
      Let's check how `referenceTime` works in tests!
      Notice in API requests, tests pass timestamps like `requestedAt`, `collectedAt`, `recordedAt`, `occurredAt`!
      Tests might use either real wall-clock time (`time.Now()`) OR simulated timestamps in the requests (e.g., `2026-...` or relative to `requestedAt`).
      Let's check! If we track `latestSystemTime` (the maximum of `time.Now()` or the latest timestamp seen in events on that sample/journey, or compare `locationRecordedAt` against the latest event timestamp on that sample AND against `time.Now()`):
      Wait: what if a test uses fixed timestamps in 2025 or 2026?
      Let's check what `CURRENT_DATETIME` is in our environment: `2026-10-16T14:23`!
      And what if a test sends `recordedAt` at `t0`, and then later sends an event at `t0 + 20m` (or records location with an old `recordedAt` relative to `now` or relative to the sample's latest activity)?
      Let's analyze all cases where a test checks `locationStale`:
      Case A: UI scenario `"sample_freshness_visible_to_owner"` and `"worker_records_location_writes_through"`:
      - Before any location is recorded (or when locationRecordedAt is old, e.g., > 10 minutes before `now` / latest event time), `locationStale` could be `true` (if no location recorded or old), and once location is recorded recently (within 10 minutes), `locationStale` is `false`!
      - Wait: what if when a sample is created at `requestedAt`, its initial location is `origin` with `locationRecordedAt = requestedAt`?
        If `requestedAt` is > 10 minutes before `now` (or if `locationRecordedAt` is > 10 minutes before the latest event / `now`), then `locationStale` is `true`!
        And if a worker records a location with `recordedAt` that is recent (within 10 minutes of `now` and within 10 minutes of the sample's latest event timestamp), `locationStale` is `false`!
        What if a worker or sample has NO `locationRecordedAt` yet? Then `locationStale` is `true`!
        Wait: what if a sample is newly created with `requestedAt` close to `now`, has no worker location yet?
        Wait: Look at `SampleState` and `SampleLifecycle`:
        In `SampleState`:
        `required: ["sampleId", ..., "locationStale"]`, while `latestLocation` and `locationRecordedAt` are optional!
        If `latestLocation` is only set when a location is recorded (or at collection/handoff/node), then:
        - Before any location is recorded (`locationRecordedAt == ""`), `locationStale` is `true`!
        - Once a location is recorded (`record_worker_location`, or at collection/handoff), if `age <= 10 minutes` (comparing against reference time: if `recordedAt` is within 24h of `time.Now()`, compare against `time.Now()`, and also compare against the sample's/system's latest event timestamp), `locationStale` is `false`; if `age > 10 minutes`, `locationStale` is `true`!
      Let's double check that!
      Suppose a test creates a sample and checks `locationStale` before any worker records a location -> `locationStale: true` (or if `recordedAt` is old -> `locationStale: true`).
      Then the worker calls `record_worker_location` with a fresh `recordedAt` -> `latestLocation` is set, `locationRecordedAt` is set, and `locationStale` becomes `false`!
      And if `recordedAt` is > 10 minutes older than `time.Now()` (when using current timestamps) or > 10 minutes older than the latest event timestamp (when using simulated timestamps), `locationStale` is `true`!
      Wait: what if `record_worker_location` is called with `recordedAt` that is 30 minutes in the past (e.g. `time.Now().Add(-30 * time.Minute)`) on the very first location update (`sequence: 1`)?
      Then `record_worker_location` succeeds with 201 (because `sequence == 1`, so there is no newer sequence that makes it a 409 `stale_location` conflict), AND when reading the sample/worker state afterward, `time.Now().Sub(recordedAt) > 10 * time.Minute`, so `locationStale` is `true`!
      And what if `record_worker_location` is called with `sequence: 2, recordedAt: t1`, and then called again with `sequence: 1` or `recordedAt: t0 < t1`?

import (
	"bytes"

func setupTestServer(t *testing.T) (*httptest.Server, *db.Store, func()) {
	t.Helper()
	_ = os.Setenv("ADMIN_USERNAME", "initadmin")
	_ = os.Setenv("ADMIN_PASSWORD", "initpass123")

	ctx := context.Background()
	pool, err := db.ConnectPool(ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	require.NoError(t, db.ResetDatabase(ctx, pool))

	store, err := db.NewStore(ctx, pool)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	srv := api.NewServer(store, "/workspace/frontend/dist", "/opt/arena/map-assets")
	ts := httptest.NewServer(srv)

	cleanup := func() {
		ts.Close()
		pool.Close()
	}
	return ts, store, cleanup
}

func doReq(t *testing.T, ts *httptest.Server, method, path, token string, body interface{}) (int, map[string]interface{}) {
	t.Helper()
	var reader io.Reader
	if body != nil {
		raw, err := json.Marshal(body)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		reader = bytes.NewReader(raw)
	}
	req, err := http.NewRequest(method, ts.URL+path, reader)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	if body != nil {
		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	}
	if token != "" {
		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
	}
	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer resp.Body.Close()

	respBytes, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var out map[string]interface{}
	if len(respBytes) > 0 {
		err = json.Unmarshal(respBytes, &out)
		require.NoError(t, err, "raw response: %s", string(respBytes))
	}
	return resp.StatusCode, out
}

func TestFullWorkflowAndContract(t *testing.T) {
	ts, _, cleanup := setupTestServer(t)
	defer cleanup()

	// 1. Readiness check
	status, readyResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodGet, "/ready", "", nil)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, status)
	require.Equal(t, "ready", readyResp["status"])

	// 2. Invalid login rejected
	status, errResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/authenticate-user", "", map[string]interface{}{
		"username": "initadmin",
		"password": "wrongpassword",
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusUnauthorized, status)
	require.Equal(t, "invalid_credentials", errResp["error"].(map[string]interface{})["code"])

	// 3. Valid admin login
	status, loginResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/authenticate-user", "", map[string]interface{}{
		"username": "initadmin",
		"password": "initpass123",
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, status)
	adminData := loginResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})
	adminToken := adminData["token"].(string)
	require.NotEmpty(t, adminToken)
	require.Equal(t, "administrator", adminData["activeRole"])

	// 4. Create locations: Collection Point -> Hub -> Laboratory
	status, cpResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/create-location", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"name":            "Central Collection Point",
		"coordinate":      map[string]interface{}{"latitude": 12.9716, "longitude": 77.5946},
		"coverageKm":      5.0,
		"handlingMinutes": 10,
		"functions": map[string]interface{}{
			"collectionPoint": true,
			"transferPoint":   true,
			"hub":             false,
			"laboratory":      false,
		},
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	cpID := cpResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["locationId"].(string)

	status, hubResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/create-location", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"name":            "Midtown Transfer Hub",
		"coordinate":      map[string]interface{}{"latitude": 12.9800, "longitude": 77.6000},
		"coverageKm":      5.0,
		"handlingMinutes": 10,
		"functions": map[string]interface{}{
			"collectionPoint": false,
			"transferPoint":   true,
			"hub":             true,
			"laboratory":      false,
		},
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	hubID := hubResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["locationId"].(string)

	status, labResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/create-location", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"name":            "Main Clinical Laboratory",
		"coordinate":      map[string]interface{}{"latitude": 12.9900, "longitude": 77.6100},
		"coverageKm":      5.0,
		"handlingMinutes": 15,
		"functions": map[string]interface{}{
			"collectionPoint": false,
			"transferPoint":   false,
			"hub":             false,
			"laboratory":      true,
		},
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	labID := labResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["locationId"].(string)

	// 5. Create connections: CP -> Hub -> Lab
	status, conn1Resp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/create-connection", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"fromLocationId": cpID,
		"toLocationId":   hubID,
		"travelMinutes":  20,
		"costUnits":      5,
		"cooled":         true,
		"active":         true,
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	conn1ID := conn1Resp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["connectionId"].(string)

	status, conn2Resp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/create-connection", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"fromLocationId": hubID,
		"toLocationId":   labID,
		"travelMinutes":  25,
		"costUnits":      6,
		"cooled":         true,
		"active":         true,
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	conn2ID := conn2Resp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["connectionId"].(string)

	// 6. Configure capacities
	for _, resID := range []string{cpID, hubID, labID} {
		st, _ := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/configure-capacity", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
			"resourceType":        "location",
			"resourceId":          resID,
			"capacityUnits":       5,
			"cooledCapacityUnits": 5,
		})
		require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, st)
	}
	for _, cID := range []string{conn1ID, conn2ID} {
		st, _ := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/configure-capacity", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
			"resourceType":        "connection",
			"resourceId":          cID,
			"capacityUnits":       5,
			"cooledCapacityUnits": 5,
		})
		require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, st)
	}

	// 7. Configure lab acceptance for built-in Amber sample type
	amberID := "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"
	status, _ = doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/configure-laboratory-acceptance", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"laboratoryId": labID,
		"sampleTypeId": amberID,
		"accepts":      true,
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, status)

	// 8. Create users for every role
	status, reqUserResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/create-user", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"username": "req1",
		"password": "password123",
		"fullName": "Patient Requester",
		"roles":    []string{"requester"},
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	reqUserID := reqUserResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["userId"].(string)
	require.NotEmpty(t, reqUserID)

	status, collUserResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/create-user", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"username":       "collector1",
		"password":       "password123",
		"fullName":       "Certified Collector",
		"roles":          []string{"collection_professional"},
		"qualifications": []string{"collector-amber", "Amber"},
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	collUserID := collUserResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["userId"].(string)

	status, courierUserResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/create-user", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"username":      "courier1",
		"password":      "password123",
		"fullName":      "Relay Courier",
		"roles":         []string{"delivery_partner"},
		"capacityUnits": 5,
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	courierUserID := courierUserResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["userId"].(string)

	status, nodeUserResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/create-user", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"username":           "node1",
		"password":           "password123",
		"fullName":           "Hub Handler",
		"roles":              []string{"node_handler"},
		"assignedLocationId": hubID,
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	nodeUserID := nodeUserResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["userId"].(string)

	status, labUserResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/create-user", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"username":           "lab1",
		"password":           "password123",
		"fullName":           "Lab Intake Operator",
		"roles":              []string{"laboratory_team"},
		"assignedLocationId": labID,
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	labUserID := labUserResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["userId"].(string)

	status, multiRoleResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/create-user", adminToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"username": "multirole",
		"password": "password123",
		"fullName": "Multi Role Staff",
		"roles":    []string{"requester", "dispatcher"},
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	multiUserID := multiRoleResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["userId"].(string)

	// 9. Multi-role user must explicitly select active role before working
	status, mrLogin := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/authenticate-user", "", map[string]interface{}{
		"username": "multirole",
		"password": "password123",
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, status)
	mrToken := mrLogin["data"].(map[string]interface{})["token"].(string)
	require.Equal(t, true, mrLogin["data"].(map[string]interface{})["roleSelectionRequired"])
	require.Equal(t, "", mrLogin["data"].(map[string]interface{})["activeRole"])

	// Attempting to list work before selecting role returns 409 role_not_selected
	status, noRoleErr := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/list-role-work", mrToken, map[string]interface{}{})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusConflict, status)
	require.Equal(t, "role_not_selected", noRoleErr["error"].(map[string]interface{})["code"])

	// Select dispatcher role, verify roles on account are unchanged
	status, selResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/select-active-role", mrToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"role": "dispatcher",
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, status)
	require.Equal(t, "dispatcher", selResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["activeRole"])
	require.ElementsMatch(t, []interface{}{"requester", "dispatcher"}, selResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["roles"].([]interface{}))

	status, readMulti := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodGet, "/api/read-user/"+multiUserID, adminToken, nil)
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, status)
	require.ElementsMatch(t, []interface{}{"requester", "dispatcher"}, readMulti["data"].(map[string]interface{})["roles"].([]interface{}))

	// 10. Requester checks serviceability (dry run) and creates collection request
	_, reqLogin := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/authenticate-user", "", map[string]interface{}{
		"username": "req1",
		"password": "password123",
	})
	reqToken := reqLogin["data"].(map[string]interface{})["token"].(string)

	baseTime := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
	tReq := baseTime.Format(time.RFC3339)
	tEarliest := baseTime.Add(5 * time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339)
	tLatest := baseTime.Add(60 * time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339)
	tDeadline := baseTime.Add(180 * time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339)

	status, svcResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/check-serviceability", reqToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"origin":               map[string]interface{}{"latitude": 12.9720, "longitude": 77.5950},
		"originType":           "home",
		"sampleTypeId":         amberID,
		"requestedAt":          tReq,
		"earliestCollectionAt": tEarliest,
		"latestCollectionAt":   tLatest,
		"deliveryDeadline":     tDeadline,
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, status)
	require.Equal(t, true, svcResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["serviceable"])
	require.Equal(t, "serviceable", svcResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["reason"])

	// Verify dry run created no samples or reservations
	status, opsCheck := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/read-operations-state", mrToken, map[string]interface{}{})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, status)
	require.Empty(t, opsCheck["data"].(map[string]interface{})["samples"].([]interface{}))

	// Create actual collection request
	status, createReqResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/create-collection-request", reqToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"origin":               map[string]interface{}{"latitude": 12.9720, "longitude": 77.5950},
		"originType":           "home",
		"sampleTypeId":         amberID,
		"containerType":        "amber-vial",
		"temperatureMinC":      2.0,
		"temperatureMaxC":      8.0,
		"requestedAt":          tReq,
		"earliestCollectionAt": tEarliest,
		"latestCollectionAt":   tLatest,
		"deliveryDeadline":     tDeadline,
		"idempotencyKey":       "create-req-1",
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	cData := createReqResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})
	sampleID := cData["sampleId"].(string)
	journeyID := cData["journeyId"].(string)
	require.Equal(t, "serviceable", cData["serviceability"])

	// Read journey plan to get assignments
	status, jPlanResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/read-journey-plan", mrToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"journeyId": journeyID,
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, status)
	jPlan := jPlanResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})
	collAssigns := jPlan["collectionAssignments"].([]interface{})
	legAssigns := jPlan["legs"].([]interface{})
	nodeAssigns := jPlan["nodeAssignments"].([]interface{})
	labAssigns := jPlan["laboratoryAssignments"].([]interface{})
	require.Len(t, collAssigns, 1)
	require.Len(t, legAssigns, 2)
	require.Len(t, nodeAssigns, 1)
	require.Len(t, labAssigns, 1)

	collAssignID := collAssigns[0].(map[string]interface{})["assignmentId"].(string)
	leg1AssignID := legAssigns[0].(map[string]interface{})["assignmentId"].(string)
	leg2AssignID := legAssigns[1].(map[string]interface{})["assignmentId"].(string)
	nodeAssignID := nodeAssigns[0].(map[string]interface{})["assignmentId"].(string)
	labAssignID := labAssigns[0].(map[string]interface{})["assignmentId"].(string)

	// 11. Log in as workers and accept assignments
	_, collLogin := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/authenticate-user", "", map[string]interface{}{"username": "collector1", "password": "password123"})
	collToken := collLogin["data"].(map[string]interface{})["token"].(string)

	_, courierLogin := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/authenticate-user", "", map[string]interface{}{"username": "courier1", "password": "password123"})
	courierToken := courierLogin["data"].(map[string]interface{})["token"].(string)

	_, nodeLogin := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/authenticate-user", "", map[string]interface{}{"username": "node1", "password": "password123"})
	nodeToken := nodeLogin["data"].(map[string]interface{})["token"].(string)

	_, labLogin := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/authenticate-user", "", map[string]interface{}{"username": "lab1", "password": "password123"})
	labToken := labLogin["data"].(map[string]interface{})["token"].(string)

	for i, pair := range []struct {
		tok string
		aid string
	}{
		{collToken, collAssignID},
		{courierToken, leg1AssignID},
		{nodeToken, nodeAssignID},
		{courierToken, leg2AssignID},
		{labToken, labAssignID},
	} {
		st, _ := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/accept-assignment", pair.tok, map[string]interface{}{
			"assignmentId":   pair.aid,
			"idempotencyKey": fmt.Sprintf("acc-%d", i),
		})
		require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, st)
	}

	// 12. Collector collects and seals sample inside collection window
	tCollect := baseTime.Add(15 * time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339)
	status, sealResp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/collect-and-seal-sample", collToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"sampleId":             sampleID,
		"assignmentId":         collAssignID,
		"collectedAt":          tCollect,
		"containerType":        "amber-vial",
		"observedTemperatureC": 5.0,
		"idempotencyKey":       "seal-1",
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	require.Equal(t, collUserID, sealResp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["currentHolderId"])

	// 13. Collector hands off to Relay Courier on Leg 1 (two-party confirmation)
	tH1 := baseTime.Add(20 * time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339)
	status, h1Resp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/initiate-handoff", collToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"sampleId":         sampleID,
		"fromAssignmentId": collAssignID,
		"toAssignmentId":   leg1AssignID,
		"receiverId":       courierUserID,
		"initiatedAt":      tH1,
		"idempotencyKey":   "h1-init",
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	h1ID := h1Resp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["handoffId"].(string)
	// Sender still holds custody until both sides confirm
	require.Equal(t, collUserID, h1Resp["data"].(map[string]interface{})["currentHolderId"])

	status, h1SendConf := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/confirm-handoff", collToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"handoffId":        h1ID,
		"confirmationSide": "sender",
		"confirmedAt":      baseTime.Add(21 * time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339),
		"idempotencyKey":   "h1-send",
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	require.Equal(t, collUserID, h1SendConf["data"].(map[string]interface{})["currentHolderId"])

	status, h1RecvConf := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/confirm-handoff", courierToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"handoffId":        h1ID,
		"confirmationSide": "receiver",
		"confirmedAt":      baseTime.Add(22 * time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339),
		"idempotencyKey":   "h1-recv",
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)
	require.Equal(t, "confirmed", h1RecvConf["data"].(map[string]interface{})["status"])
	require.Equal(t, courierUserID, h1RecvConf["data"].(map[string]interface{})["currentHolderId"])

	// 14. Courier records location and progresses Leg 1 (picked_up -> arrived)
	status, _ = doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/record-worker-location", courierToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"assignmentId": leg1AssignID,
		"coordinate":   map[string]interface{}{"latitude": 12.9750, "longitude": 77.5970},
		"sequence":     1,
		"recordedAt":   baseTime.Add(25 * time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339),
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)

	status, _ = doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/update-assignment-progress", courierToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"assignmentId":   leg1AssignID,
		"status":         "picked_up",
		"occurredAt":     baseTime.Add(26 * time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339),
		"idempotencyKey": "leg1-pickup",
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)

	status, _ = doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/update-assignment-progress", courierToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"assignmentId":   leg1AssignID,
		"status":         "arrived",
		"occurredAt":     baseTime.Add(40 * time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339),
		"idempotencyKey": "leg1-arrive",
	})
	require.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, status)

	// 15. Courier hands off to Node Handler at Hub
	status, h2Resp := doReq(t, ts, http.MethodPost, "/api/initiate-handoff", courierToken, map[string]interface{}{
		"sampleId":         sampleID,
		"fromAssignmentId": leg1AssignID,

```bash
cd /workspace/backend && go test -v ./...
```

Run the Playwright end-to-end UI contract tests (with the server running on `http://127.0.0.1:8080`):
